title: The Unfinished Manuscript
text:
Postmodern fiction frequently abandons the pretence of a single, authoritative voice. Its narrators may contradict themselves, interrupt the story to address the reader directly, or admit that the events they describe are invented. Such devices are not mere ornaments; they challenge the assumption that a text can transparently convey a fixed truth. Readers are therefore obliged to assemble meaning from fragments rather than receive it passively.

Critics have long debated whether this experimentation is an authentic response to a fractured world or an intellectual game detached from human experience. Supporters argue that the instability of the text mirrors the instability of modern life. Detractors respond that obscurity can become a fashionable mask for emptiness. Whichever view one adopts, the experimental novel compels readers to examine their own habits of interpretation.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what do postmodern narrators sometimes do?
options: They speak to the reader directly and admit the events are invented
They present one fixed and unquestioned truth
They avoid any contradiction in the story
They describe the events in strict chronological order

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what do supporters of this experimentation argue?
options: The instability of the text mirrors the instability of modern life
The experimental novel has no connection to human experience
Obscurity is a useful way to hide emptiness
Readers should never interpret a text for themselves

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of traditional narration, based on the first paragraph?
options: The author suggests that claiming a single authoritative voice is questionable
The author believes that a single voice always conveys truth transparently
The author thinks readers should avoid fragments
The author considers chronology essential to meaning

questions.text: The final sentence of the passage implies that experimental fiction is valuable mainly because it
options: encourages readers to reflect on how they interpret texts
provides a fixed and final truth about the world
removes the need for any interpretation

vocabulary.definition: a false appearance or claim that something is true
decorative features added for beauty, not essential to the main purpose
the state of being unsteady or constantly changing
the quality of being hard to understand or unclear

paragraph_translations: Postmodern kurgu, tek ve yetkili bir anlatıcı sesi yanılsamasını sık sık bırakır. Anlatıcıları kendi kendileriyle çelişebilir, hikayeyi kesip okuyucuya doğrudan seslenebilir ya da anlattıkları olayların uydurulduğunu kabul edebilir. Bu araçlar yalnızca süs değildir; bir metnin sabit bir gerçeği şeffaf biçimde aktarabileceği varsayımını sorgular. Bu nedenle okuyucular, anlamı pasif biçimde almak yerine parçalardan kendileri oluşturmak zorunda kalır.

Eleştirmenler, bu deneyselliğin parçalanmış bir dünyaya özgün bir tepki mi yoksa insan deneyiminden kopuk bir entelektüel oyun mu olduğunu uzun süredir tartışmaktadır. Destekleyenler, metnin istikrarsızlığının modern yaşamın istikrarsızlığını yansıttığını savunur. Karşı çıkanlar ise belirsizliğin boşluğu örten moda bir maske haline gelebileceğini yanıtlar. Hangi görüşü benimsenirse benimsensin, deneysel roman okuyucuları kendi yorumlama alışkanlıklarını sorgulamaya zorlar.
